mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen steadily for four consecutive weeks (-48.7 to -41.3), indicating a persistent reopening trend driven by gradual recovery of consumer activity. This monotonic improvement is expected to continue linearly over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the upward trend stalled or reversed.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -72.1 to -69.0 over four weeks, suggesting restored commuting and travel capacity that feeds directly into retail footfall. If TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC should rise in the following 1-2 weeks as transit-dependent shoppers return.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -72.1 to -69.0 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the 1-2 weeks following a TRANSIT improvement exceeding 2 points, or declines despite continued TRANSIT gains.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has climbed from -43.0 to -37.7, signaling loosening of work-from-home mandates or office reopening policy. If WORKPLACES crosses above -35 within the next two weeks, this policy-driven return to offices will spill over into adjacent retail and recreation visits via lunch-hour and after-work shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -43.0 to -37.7 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 2 weeks after WORKPLACES crosses -35, or WORKPLACES crosses but RETAIL_REC stagnates or falls.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 22.3 to 20.0 over four weeks, indicating reduced time spent at home and a behavioral shift toward outside activity. Combined with rising PARKS mobility, this suggests increased willingness for discretionary outings, which should also lift retail and recreation visits as people re-engage with public spaces together.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell each week while PARKS rose each week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase even though RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and PARKS continues to rise jointly over the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The pace of RETAIL_REC recovery is decelerating: weekly gains shrank from +2.6 (t-3w to t-2w) to +1.8 (t-2w to t-1w) to +3.0 (t-1w to t-0w), showing an unstable, non-monotonic deceleration pattern. If this deceleration trend resumes and weekly gains fall below 1.5 points, momentum will stall and RETAIL_REC growth will flatten or reverse over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC gain falls below 1.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:weekly RETAIL_REC gains were 2.6, 1.8, 3.0 showing inconsistent momentum
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to post weekly gains above 1.5 points consistently over the next 4 weeks despite the flagged deceleration signal.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved sharply from -11.6 to -5.0, nearing baseline, which signals strong recovery of essential-goods foot traffic. This leading indicator of normalized shopping behavior typically precedes recovery in discretionary retail and recreation visits within 1-2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved by 6.6 points over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following continued GROCERY_PHARM improvement toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: All six mobility categories show simultaneous improvement toward baseline, consistent with a coordinated policy relaxation regime (e.g., lifted curfews or capacity limits). In such a regime, cross-category co-movement amplifies retail recovery beyond what any single series predicts, because eased restrictions on TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly unlock retail access.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved monotonically over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform a single-series forecast despite continued joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, falling instead into stagnation or decline.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-September, approaching the start of India's festive shopping season (Navratri/Durga Puja/Diwali lead-up typically beginning late September to October). Seasonal anticipatory shopping behavior should amplify the existing recovery trend in RETAIL_REC, producing an above-trend acceleration in the next 4 weeks regardless of other mobility signals.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-09-15, preceding the festive shopping season in Delhi
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over the next 4 weeks does not exceed the growth rate observed over the prior 4 weeks, indicating no seasonal acceleration occurred.
